primary.poolable_reason: ENOXAPARIN IS THE INTERVENTION IN ONLY ONE OF THREE TRIALS. NCT00362232 tests RIVAROXABAN against enoxaparin after orthopaedic surgery -- a rivaroxaban trial. NCT02366871 tests APIXABAN against enoxaparin in gynaecologic cancer -- an apixaban trial. In both, enoxaparin sits in the ACTIVE_COMPARATOR arm. Only NCT01573169 tests enoxaparin itself, against graduated compression stockings, in haemorrhagic stroke. So this is k=1 for the question the title asks, and it is the OLMESARTAN shape in part: two of the three trials belong to other drugs.

primary.what_this_verdict_does_not_establish: NOT that any of these trials is poor -- each is registered, randomised where it says so, and reports its primary. NOT that the drug is ineffective. NOT that no poolable question exists in this area: only that the question this page's title asks cannot be answered by pooling the trials this page carries. If a further eligible trial is identified, this verdict should be revisited.
